paper_metadata.title: Quantum Data Learning of Topological-to-Ferromagnetic Phase Transitions in the 2+1D Toric Code Loop Gas Model

summary: The paper studies gate-based quantum data learning on the 2+1D toric-code loop-gas model using VQE-prepared ground states on lattices of size 2x2, 2x3, 3x3, and 4x3 (4, 7, 12, and 17 qubits). The QCNN achieves 100% classification accuracy on three lattice sizes and 96% on 3x3, with finite-size scaling yielding xc(infty)=0.2518 ± 0.0260, close to the QMC benchmark xc≈0.25; unsupervised quantum k-means estimates the transition at 0.262(2), 0.272(2), 0.282(2), and 0.277(2) across the four lattices.

experiments.description: Supervised quantum data learning of phase classification and phase-boundary estimation for the 2+1D toric-code loop-gas model using a QCNN trained on VQE-generated ground states across four lattice sizes.

algorithm.variant: quantum convolutional neural network (QCNN) for supervised phase classification
algorithm.convergence_criteria: 100 epochs; convergence monitored by loss stabilization (successive loss values vary by less than 1e-3 in Appendix C)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: quantum ground states |psi_x> prepared by VQE are fed directly into the QCNN; no classical feature encoding is used
problem_formulation.objective_function: binary phase classification between topologically ordered (-1) and ferromagnetically ordered (+1) phases; QCNN output y_out = Tr[Z_out U_QCNN |psi_x><psi_x| U_QCNN^†]
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H(x) = (1 - x) H_TCM - x sum_i sigma^z_i

problem_instance.description: 2+1D toric-code loop-gas model in a longitudinal magnetic field; phase transition from topological to ferromagnetic order

dataset_specification.description: ground states generated for lattice sizes 2x2, 2x3, 3x3, 4x3; half sampled from x in [0, xc], half from x in [xc+1e-2, 1]; xc approx 0.25 from QMC

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: ground states generated by VQE on a grid of field values x; labels assigned using approximate critical point xc≈0.25; random 80/20 split for classification and physics-aware split excluding 0.2<=x<=0.4 for transition estimation
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: classification accuracy on held-out test set; phase flip-interval estimator x'_c from QCNN decision boundary; repeated training for different sample sizes; finite-size scaling across four lattice sizes

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: VQE-generated ground states used as inputs; labels assigned from approximate critical point; random split or physics-aware split
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: phase flip-interval extracted from QCNN output versus field parameter; finite-size scaling fit x'_c(L)=x_c(infty)+a/L_eff

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: decreasing and stabilizing; CNNs converge faster than QCNNs

speedup_claims.factor: more reliable transition estimates than classical CNN and logistic regression; more sample-efficient than other baselines
speedup_claims.conditions: on toric-code loop-gas datasets across lattice sizes 2x2, 2x3, 3x3, 4x3; especially in the 4x3 lattice and with limited training samples
speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic complexity or wall-clock speedup is reported; claim is based on accuracy/estimation quality and sample efficiency.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No practical quantum advantage resources are demonstrated; the study is a small-scale simulated QCNN on 4- to 17-qubit toric-code states.
limiting_factors: No hardware execution on a QPU
Problem sizes are small (up to 4x3 lattice / 17 qubits)
Classical CNN and logistic regression baselines are competitive and sometimes worse, but no quantum advantage is established

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper reports classical simulation / VQE-generated states and does not name a physical QPU.
num_qubits reported from the smallest lattice size explicitly stated in the paper (2x2 lattice = 4 qubits); the study spans 4, 7, 12, and 17 qubits across lattice sizes.
circuit depth not explicitly reported for the QCNN; only the layered architecture is described.
speedup order not characterized asymptotically in the paper.

The paper reports QCNN phase classification accuracy of 100% on 2x2, 2x3, and 4x3 lattices and 96% on 3x3, but also reports that classical CNN and logistic regression baselines are compared and that classical models can capture the broad phase structure.
Finite-size scaling gives QCNN xc(infty)=0.2518 ± 0.026, close to the QMC benchmark xc≈0.25, but this is not a demonstrated computational advantage.

experiments.description: Unsupervised quantum k-means clustering of VQE-generated toric-code ground states to identify the topological-to-ferromagnetic phase boundary without labels.

algorithm.variant: quantum k-means clustering based on state overlaps / fidelity

problem_formulation.encoding_details: quantum states |psi_i> are clustered directly using pairwise overlaps; no classical feature encoding
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize total intra-cluster distance L = sum_c sum_{i in C_c} d^2(psi_i, psi_m_c) with d(psi_i,psi_j)=sqrt(2(1-F(psi_i,psi_j)))
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H(x) = (1 - x) H_TCM - x sum_i sigma^z_i

problem_instance.description: Same toric-code loop-gas dataset as the supervised experiment; unsupervised phase discovery across four lattice sizes

dataset_specification.description: ground states for 2x2, 2x3, 3x3, 4x3 lattices; x sampled across [0,1] with balanced phase coverage

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: pairwise fidelities computed between quantum states; cluster labels oriented so small-x states correspond to topological phase
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: cluster assignments analyzed as a function of x; phase flip-interval estimator x_hat_c extracted; compared against QMC benchmark and QCNN estimates

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: pairwise state fidelities computed from VQE-generated states
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: cluster-flip interval extracted from cluster labels versus field parameter; finite-size scaling performed

speedup_claims.conditions: unsupervised clustering on VQE-generated toric-code ground states
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an algorithmic advantage rather than a runtime speedup; no asymptotic or wall-clock speedup is reported.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No advantage resources are demonstrated; the method is an unsupervised clustering proof-of-principle on small simulated datasets.
limiting_factors: No classical runtime comparison establishing superiority
Estimated critical points are slightly above the QMC benchmark

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper presents a simulated VQE-generated dataset and no physical quantum device is named.
num_qubits reported from the smallest lattice size explicitly stated in the paper (2x2 lattice = 4 qubits); the study spans 4, 7, 12, and 17 qubits across lattice sizes.
circuit depth not reported for the quantum k-means procedure; only the overlap-based clustering method is described.
speedup order not characterized asymptotically in the paper.
The paper reports unsupervised phase boundary estimates of 0.262(2), 0.272(2), 0.282(2), and 0.277(2) for 2x2, 2x3, 3x3, and 4x3 lattices, respectively.
The method requires no labels, but the paper does not claim a practical advantage over classical methods.

experiments.description: Variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) ground-state preparation of the toric-code loop-gas model using a parametrized loop-gas circuit (PLGC) across multiple lattice sizes and field values.

algorithm.variant: VQE with parametrized loop-gas circuit (PLGC) ansatz
algorithm.convergence_criteria: 500 optimization steps per trial; best final-energy trial retained
algorithm.parameter_initialization: random angles theta_p uniformly sampled in [0, 2pi)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: PLGC acts on a product state |0>^N and generates weighted superpositions of closed-loop configurations; one unitary per plaquette
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: physics-motivated ansatz restricts search to loop-gas subspace
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H(x) = (1 - x) H_TCM - x sum_i sigma^z_i

problem_instance.description: Ground-state preparation for the 2+1D toric-code loop-gas model in a magnetic field

dataset_specification.description: ground states generated for x in [0,1] on lattices 2x2, 2x3, 3x3, 4x3

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: VQE run at each x value; ten independent trials per x; lowest-energy parameters retained; compared against exact diagonalization for validation
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: energy per qubit and magnetization per qubit compared with exact diagonalization; accuracy of generated states assessed visually and by agreement with ED

implementation_details.classical_solver: exact diagonalization used only as benchmark
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: random initialization of PLGC parameters; repeated trials per x
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: select lowest-energy trial; compute energy per qubit and magnetization per qubit

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: energy minimized over SPSA iterations; best trial retained

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper validates VQE-generated states against exact diagonalization but does not claim a speedup.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: VQE ground-state preparation is used as a state-preparation subroutine; no advantage claim is made for VQE itself in this paper.
limiting_factors: The paper uses VQE as a preparation method, not as a benchmarked optimization advantage
No comparison against classical ground-state solvers is framed as a quantum advantage result
The study is limited to small lattices and simulation

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper reports VQE-generated states and exact diagonalization comparisons, with no physical QPU named.
num_qubits reported from the smallest lattice size explicitly stated in the paper (2x2 lattice = 4 qubits); the study spans 4, 7, 12, and 17 qubits across lattice sizes.
circuit depth not explicitly reported for the PLGC ansatz; only the plaquette-wise construction is described.
speedup order not characterized asymptotically in the paper.

The paper reports that VQE-generated ground states agree almost perfectly with exact diagonalization for energy per qubit and magnetization, but this is a validation of state preparation rather than an advantage claim.
